title: SIL assessment procedure
note: DRAFT. Written as a starting point for a client discipline engineer to confirm or change (W5b-10, #547). The source standards are not held, so no clause number below has been checked against the standard's text; each is the author's reading of its table of contents. Nothing here is a finding until a signed-off playbook says so.

elements.title: Purpose, scope and applicable standards
elements.expects: The procedure says what the assessment covers and names the standards it follows.

elements.title: Roles and competence
elements.expects: The roles in the assessment and the competence expected of the people are stated.

elements.title: Input from the hazard and risk assessment
elements.expects: The assessment starts from the results of the hazard and risk assessment (HAZOP).

elements.title: Tolerable risk criteria
elements.expects: The tolerable risk (the target) is defined.

elements.title: SIL determination method
elements.expects: The method used to determine the SIL is named and described (LOPA, risk graph, ...).

elements.title: Independent protection layers and their credit
elements.expects: The independent protection layers and the credit given to each are addressed.

elements.title: Safety instrumented functions and their target SIL
elements.expects: Each safety instrumented function (SIF) is identified and its target SIL recorded.

elements.title: Demand mode, proof test and PFD
elements.expects: The demand mode, proof-test interval and the PFD calculation are addressed.

elements.title: Verification and independent review
elements.expects: The assessment is verified or independently reviewed.

elements.title: Safety requirements specification and records
elements.expects: The result feeds a safety requirements specification and the records are kept.

elements.title: Data and assumptions
elements.expects: The failure-rate data and the assumptions behind the numbers are stated.

elements.title: Revalidation and management of change
elements.expects: The procedure says when the assessment is repeated or reviewed.
